meta.title: Step 5D Pilot — Probability & Statistics Laboratory (construction-lab 1.5.0)
meta.subject: Mathematics (NaCCA Primary/JHS & Cambridge IGCSE 0580 / AS 9709 S1)
meta.topic: DataStatsLab v1.5.0 Verification (20 slides, 20 curriculum activities)

slides.title: 1. Primary Coin Experiment
slides.purpose: NaCCA B4 fair coin toss experiment.
onScreenText: Fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes
Experimental frequency approaches 0.5 over many tosses

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">1. Primary Fair Coin Experiment</text></svg>

narration.script: Toss the virtual Ghana cedi coin and compare experimental heads to the theoretical probability of one half.

interactive.title: Fair Coin Toss Experiment
interactive.instructions: Run trials and enter the theoretical probability of Heads.

slides.title: 2. Primary Pictogram & Frequency Table
slides.purpose: NaCCA B4 fictional fruit survey pictogram.
onScreenText: Read frequencies from a categorical pictogram

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">2. Primary Pictogram & Frequency</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the total number of pupils who chose Mango in this fictional class survey.

keyIdeas: Pictograms represent categorical frequencies.

interactive.title: Class Favourite Fruit Pictogram
interactive.instructions: How many learners chose Mango?

slides.title: 3. Primary Mode and Range
slides.purpose: Find the mode of a small fictional quiz score list.
onScreenText: Mode is the most frequent value
Range = Max − Min

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">3. Primary Mode & Range</text></svg>

narration.script: Identify the mode of the fictional spelling scores.

keyIdeas: Mode appears most often.

interactive.title: Find the Mode
interactive.instructions: Enter the modal score from the sorted list.

slides.title: 4. JHS Fair Six-Sided Die Experiment
slides.purpose: Explore P(6) on a fair die.
onScreenText: P(rolling a 6) = 1/6 ≈ 0.167

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">4. JHS Fair Die Experiment</text></svg>

narration.script: Roll the virtual die and enter the theoretical probability of rolling a six.

interactive.title: Fair 6-Sided Die Experiment
interactive.instructions: Enter P(6) as a fraction (1/6) or decimal (0.167).

slides.title: 5. JHS Weighted Spinner Probabilities
slides.purpose: Unequal spinner sectors (weights 3, 2, 1).
onScreenText: Sector probabilities proportional to angle/weight

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fffbeb"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#92400e">5. JHS Weighted Spinner</text></svg>

narration.script: Calculate the probability of landing on Red when Red covers 3 of 6 equal sectors.

keyIdeas: Weight 3 out of total 6 gives P(Red) = 3/6 = 0.5.

interactive.title: Weighted Ghana-Colours Spinner
interactive.instructions: Find the theoretical probability of landing on Red.

slides.title: 6. JHS Mean, Median & Mode
slides.purpose: Compute the exact median of an even-sized dataset.
onScreenText: Sort values first; for even n average the two middle values

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">6. JHS Mean, Median & Mode</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the exact median of the six test marks.

interactive.title: Find the Exact Median
interactive.instructions: Compute the median of this 6-item fictional dataset.

slides.title: 7. Fictional Ghanaian Market Sales (Bar Chart)
slides.purpose: Read fictional Makola market daily yam sales.
onScreenText: Bar charts compare discrete categories with gaps between bars

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">7. Ghanaian Market Sales Bar Chart</text></svg>

narration.script: Read Friday's fictional yam tuber sales from the bar chart.

keyIdeas: Bar charts display discrete categorical totals.

interactive.title: Fictional Market Yam Sales (Mon–Fri)
interactive.instructions: How many yam tubers were sold on Friday?

slides.title: 8. Fictional School Attendance (Frequency Table Mean)
slides.purpose: Calculate weighted mean from a fictional attendance frequency table.
onScreenText: Mean = Σ(value × frequency) / Σ(frequency)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">8. Fictional School Attendance Mean</text></svg>

narration.script: Calculate the mean days attended from this fictional anonymised class frequency table.

keyIdeas: Divide Σfx by total frequency Σf, not by the number of rows.

commonMisconceptions: Dividing by number of rows instead of total frequency

interactive.title: Mean Weekly Days Attended (Fictional Dataset)
interactive.instructions: Calculate the mean days attended across all 20 fictional pupils.

slides.title: 9. Kumasi Monthly Rainfall Range (Fictional)
slides.purpose: Compute the range of monthly rainfall observations (mm).
onScreenText: Range = Maximum − Minimum

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#ecfeff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#155e75">9. Fictional Rainfall Observations</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the range of the fictional monthly rainfall readings in millimetres.

keyIdeas: Range measures total spread: 210 − 25 = 185 mm.

commonMisconceptions: Writing '25 to 210' instead of the difference 185

interactive.title: Range of Monthly Rainfall (mm)
interactive.instructions: Compute the range (Max − Min) in mm.

slides.title: 10. Sampling WITH Replacement (Independent)
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 two draws from a bag of 3 Red, 2 Blue counters with replacement.
onScreenText: With replacement: P(Red, Red) = (3/5) × (3/5) = 9/25 = 0.36

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">10. Sampling WITH Replacement</text></svg>

narration.script: Draw two counters with replacement and compute P(both Red).

keyIdeas: Population stays 5 on the second draw.

interactive.title: Two Counters WITH Replacement
interactive.instructions: Find P(Red then Red) with replacement (9/25 or 0.36).

slides.title: 11. Sampling WITHOUT Replacement (Dependent)
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 two draws from 3 Red, 2 Blue counters WITHOUT replacement.
onScreenText: Without replacement: P(Red, Red) = (3/5) × (2/4) = 6/20 = 0.30

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fef2f2"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#991b1b">11. Sampling WITHOUT Replacement</text></svg>

narration.script: Without replacement, the remaining counters drop to 4 after the first draw. Find P(both Red).

keyIdeas: Dependent events update the remaining population.

interactive.title: Two Counters WITHOUT Replacement
interactive.instructions: Find P(Red then Red) without replacement (3/10 or 0.3).

slides.title: 12. Compound Probability — Sum of Two Dice = 7
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 two-dice sample space (6/36 = 1/6).
onScreenText: 36 equally likely pairs; 6 pairs sum to 7 → P = 6/36 = 1/6

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">12. Compound Probability (2 Dice)</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the theoretical probability that two fair dice sum to 7.

keyIdeas: 6 out of 36 outcomes give a sum of 7.

interactive.title: Two Fair Dice — Sum Equals 7
interactive.instructions: Enter P(sum = 7) as 1/6 or 0.167.

slides.title: 13. Grouped-Data Estimated Mean
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 estimated mean using class midpoints.
onScreenText: Grouped data gives an ESTIMATE using class midpoints

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">13. Grouped-Data Estimated Mean</text></svg>

narration.script: Use the class midpoints to calculate the estimated mean of this grouped dataset.

keyIdeas: Grouped mean is an estimate because exact raw values are unknown.

commonMisconceptions: Using upper bounds instead of midpoints

interactive.title: Estimate the Mean from Grouped Data
interactive.instructions: Compute Σ(midpoint × f) / Σf.

slides.title: 14. Unequal-Width Histogram (Frequency Density)
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 / AS 9709 histogram where bar height = frequency density.
onScreenText: Frequency Density = Frequency ÷ Class Width
Bar Area = Frequency

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">14. Unequal-Width Histogram</text></svg>

narration.script: Find the frequency density of the 20 to 40 class (frequency 30, width 20).

keyIdeas: Unequal class widths require Frequency Density on the y-axis.

commonMisconceptions: Plotting raw frequency on unequal widths

interactive.title: Unequal-Width Histogram — Frequency Density
interactive.instructions: Enter the frequency density of the 20–40 class.
interactive.fallbackText: Class 20–40 has width 20 and frequency 30 → FD = 30/20 = 1.5.

slides.title: 15. Cumulative Frequency Graph
slides.purpose: IGCSE 0580 non-decreasing cumulative frequency curve.
onScreenText: Plot cumulative frequency at class UPPER bounds

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdfa"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#134e4a">15. Cumulative Frequency Graph</text></svg>

narration.script: Read the cumulative frequency at upper bound 20.

keyIdeas: Cumulative frequency is always monotonically non-decreasing.

commonMisconceptions: Plotting at midpoints instead of upper bounds

interactive.title: Cumulative Frequency Curve
interactive.instructions: What is the cumulative frequency at x = 20?

slides.title: 16. Quartiles & Box Plot
slides.purpose: IGCSE/AS box plot with explicit quartile convention.
onScreenText: IQR = Q₃ − Q₁
Box spans Q₁ to Q₃ with median inside

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">16. Quartiles & Box Plot</text></svg>

narration.script: Inspect the box plot and enter the interquartile range Q3 minus Q1.

keyIdeas: IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of data.

interactive.title: Box Plot & Interquartile Range
interactive.instructions: Find the IQR (Q3 − Q1) using Tukey Exclusive quartiles (Q1=5, Q3=13).

slides.title: 17. Population vs Sample Standard Deviation
slides.purpose: AS 9709 S1 explicit distinction between σ (÷ N) and s (÷ N−1).
onScreenText: Population SD divides by N; Sample SD divides by N − 1

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#faf5ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#581c87">17. Population vs Sample SD</text></svg>

narration.script: Calculate the population standard deviation of [2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9].

interactive.title: Population Standard Deviation (σ)
interactive.instructions: Calculate the exact population standard deviation σ (divide by N = 8).

slides.title: 18. Scatterplot & Pearson Correlation
slides.purpose: AS 9709 scatterplot exploring positive linear correlation and correlation != causation.
onScreenText: r close to +1 indicates strong positive linear correlation
Correlation does NOT prove causation

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">18. Scatterplot & Correlation</text></svg>

narration.script: Inspect the perfectly collinear points and enter Pearson r.

keyIdeas: Perfect positive line y = 2x + 1 has r = 1.

interactive.title: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (r)
interactive.instructions: Enter Pearson r for these points.
interactive.fallbackText: All points lie on y = 2x + 1, so r = 1.

slides.title: 19. Outlier Effects on Mean vs Median
slides.purpose: Investigate how an outlier pulls the mean strongly while barely affecting the median.
onScreenText: Toggle the outlier (100) to see how mean jumps while median stays stable

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fef2f2"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#991b1b">19. Outlier Effects on Mean</text></svg>

narration.script: Toggle the outlier value 100 and observe how the mean shifts dramatically.

keyIdeas: The mean is sensitive to extreme outliers; the median is resistant.

commonMisconceptions: Outliers affect mean and median equally

interactive.title: Outlier Investigation (Base Mean = 14)
interactive.instructions: Compute the mean of the base dataset (or toggle the outlier 100 to compare!).
interactive.fallbackText: Base mean = 14; with outlier 100, mean jumps to 28.33.

slides.title: 20. Linear Regression & Extrapolation Caution
slides.purpose: AS 9709 simple linear regression prediction and extrapolation warning.
onScreenText: Line of best fit: y = mx + c
Extrapolation outside observed x-range can be unreliable

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdfa"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#134e4a">20. Linear Regression & Extrapolation</text></svg>

narration.script: Use the regression line y = 2x + 1 to predict y at x = 6, noting that x = 6 is an extrapolation.

keyIdeas: Predictions outside [minX, maxX] are extrapolations and must be treated cautiously.

commonMisconceptions: Extrapolation is always as reliable as interpolation

interactive.title: Linear Regression Prediction (Extrapolation at x = 6)
interactive.instructions: Predict y when x = 6 using the regression line y = 2x + 1.
